Alarms are logged in the SCADA event log with timestamp, description, and acknowledge/re-send status. All critical alarms are also sent as SMS to the O&M duty engineer's mobile phone (two numbers on rotation). - No automatic water suppression inside inverter house due to electrical risk. External hydrant point at 25 m distance, with 30 m hose.
- Combiner boxes: no active suppression, fuse protection only. Vegetation clearance maintained at 5 m around all combiner boxes and cable trenches.

**4. SCADA, MONITORING AND CONTROL**

**4.1 SCADA Architecture**

| RTU Type | ABB RTU560, installed in inverter house |
| Communication Protocol | IEC 60870-5-104 (to dispatch), Modbus TCP (to inverters) |
| Fieldbus | Fibre optic ring, 24-core SM, 2 redundant paths |
| Weather Station | Vaisala WTX520, mounted on met mast (height 5 m) |
| Met Mast Location | North-west corner, adjacent to row 2, string 4 |
| Data Logger | Campbell Scientific CR1000X, backup to local SD card |
| Sampling Rate | 5 seconds (electrical), 1 minute (meteorological) |
| Reporting Interval | 15-minute averaged values to dispatch, 5-minute to O&M office |

**4.2 Data Points Monitored**

- Per inverter: AC power (kW), DC power (kW), DC voltage (V), DC current (A), AC voltage (V), AC current (A), frequency (Hz), power factor, reactive power (kVAr), inverter temperature (°C), heat sink temperature (°C), DC/AC ratio, daily energy (kWh), total energy (MWh), operating status, fault codes.
- Per combiner box: DC current (A) per string, string voltage (V), fuse status, surge arrester status.
- Plant level: active power (MW), reactive power (MVAr), grid frequency (Hz), grid voltage (V) at 11kV busbar, ambient temperature (°C), module temperature (°C) via 2 PT100 sensors on representative modules, wind speed (m/s), wind direction, irradiance (W/m²) on plane-of-array (POA) and global horizontal (GHI), rainfall (mm).
- Metering: 11kV export/import kWh and kVArh, bidirectional, accuracy class 0.2s, CT/VT ratio recorded in meter register.

**4.3 Alarm Management**

Alarm levels are defined as:

| Level | Priority | Response Time | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 – Critical | Immediate | < 15 minutes | Inverter trip, grid over/under voltage, fire alarm |
| 2 – High | < 1 hour | < 4 hours | String fault, communication loss to RTU |
| 3 – Medium | < 8 hours | < 24 hours | Module temperature high, soiling alarm |
| 4 – Low | < 72 hours | < 7 days | Data logger clock drift, spare part low stock |

Alarms are logged in the SCADA event log with timestamp, description, and acknowledge/re-send status. All critical alarms are also sent as SMS to the O&M duty engineer's mobile phone (two numbers on rotation). A weekly alarm summary is generated every Monday 06:00 and emailed to the plant manager and the cooperative's technical committee.

**5. PROTECTION AND SAFETY SYSTEMS**

**5.1 DC Side Protection**

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| String Fuses | 15 A gPV, 1100 V DC, in combiner boxes |
| Combiner Box Surge Arresters | Type 2, 600 V DC, 40 kA, with thermal disconnector |

| PV Array Frame Earthing | 70 mm² bare copper, connected to earth grid at 4 points per block |
| String Cable | 4 mm² single-core, double-insulated, UV resistant, rated 1.8 kV DC |

**5.2 AC Side Protection**

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Inverter AC Breaker | 400 A, 3-pole, 690 V AC, with shunt trip |
| Transformer Protection | 11kV SF6 load-break switch, 800 kVA, with overcurrent relay (50/51), earth fault relay (50N/51N) |
| 11kV Incomer Breaker | Vacuum circuit breaker, 630 A, 25 kA, with distance protection (21) and directional earth fault (67N) |
| Grid Protection Relay | MiCOM P143, over/under voltage (27/59), over/under frequency (81O/U), rate of change of frequency (81R), vector shift (78) |
| Interconnection Point | 11kV busbar at Kano Distribution Substation, Feeder KA-04 |

**5.3 Fire Detection and Suppression**

- Inverter house: 2 optical smoke detectors, 1 heat detector, connected to local alarm panel with relay output to SCADA. Manual call points at both doors.
- Fire extinguishers: 4 × 6 kg CO2 (electrical), 2 × 9 kg dry powder (general), located at inverter house entrance and transformer plinth.
- No automatic water suppression inside inverter house due to electrical risk. External hydrant point at 25 m distance, with 30 m hose.
- Combiner boxes: no active suppression, fuse protection only. Vegetation clearance maintained at 5 m around all combiner boxes and cable trenches.

documents.title: Port Harcourt Battery Storage – Engineering Datasheet
documents.content:
IMPORTANT: This datasheet is the current controlled reference for the Port Harcourt Battery
Storage system. All field maintenance actions, capacity tests, and safety planning must be
checked against this revision. Superseded revisions are archived in the site document control
register (see Rev. 0, dated 2021-11-02, for historical values that have since been revised).

1. SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION

| Item | Value | Remarks |
|------|-------|---------|
| Facility name | Port Harcourt Battery Storage | Also referred to as "PH Battery" or "PHBS" in site logs. |
| Location | Trans-Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State | GPS: 4.8156° N, 7.0498° E (approx.) |
| Grid connection | 33 kV feeder, PHEDC substation (Tie-in point: PHBS-33-01) | Interconnection agreement ref: NDRC/PHEDC/2019-014 |
| Commissioning date | 2021-11-15 | Original energisation. |
| Primary function | Grid frequency regulation, peak shaving, solar PV firming | Hybrid plant adjacent: 5 MWp PV. |
| Owner/Operator | Niger Delta Renewables Cooperative (NDRC) | O&M contract: NDRC/OM/2022-007 (3-yr term). |

2. BATTERY CHEMISTRY & CELL CONFIGURATION

3. RATED POWER & ENERGY CAPACITY

| Parameter | Value | Condition / Status |
|-----------|-------|--------------------|
| Rated AC power output | 10 MW | At inverter terminals, cos φ = 0.95 (lag). |
| Rated DC power input | 11.2 MW | Max charging power at 1C on DC side. |
| Storage capacity (useable) | 20 MWh | Current controlled value per Rev. 1.0. This is the nameplate capacity for the installed 40-rack configuration. |
| Useable energy window | 18 MWh | 90% DoD operational limit (set for cycle life). |
| Auxiliary consumption | 45 kW (avg) | HVAC, BMS, lighting, controls. |
| Round-trip efficiency | 88% (AC-to-AC) | Measured during commissioning; re-test due 2024. |
| Max continuous discharge duration | 2 hours at 10 MW | Limited by useable energy window. |

Note: The datasheet notes Port Harcourt Battery Storage capacity_mwh 20. Record status: current. This value is
current and supersedes the provisional 18 MWh figure listed in Rev. 0 (which was a
conservative estimate pending final rack commissioning). No further derating is applied.

4. POWER CONVERSION SYSTEM (PCS)

| Parameter | Specification | Remarks |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| Inverter type | IGBT-based, 4-quadrant | Bidirectional. |
| Number of PCS units | 5 × 2 MW | Each unit tied to one 20-ft container. |
| DC input voltage range | 600 – 1000 V DC | MPPT for PV not used; fixed DC link. |
| AC output voltage | 3300 V AC, 3-phase | Step-up transformer to 33 kV outside container. |
| Overload capability | 110% for 10 s | For grid fault ride-through. |
| Reactive power range | ± 5 MVAr | At rated active power. |
| Grid code compliance | Nigerian Grid Code (2019) – subsections 5.4, 7.2 | Frequency range 49.5–50.5 Hz. |

5. BATTERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (BMS)

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Topology | 3-tier: Cell Module Controller (CMC) → Rack Controller (RC) → Master BMS. |
| Monitoring | Cell voltage (± 2 mV), temperature (each module), pack current. |
| Protection | Over-voltage, under-voltage, over-temp, over-current, short-circuit, insulation fault. |
| Balancing | Passive balancing at module level (100 mA bleed). |
| State estimation | SOC (Coulomb-counting + OCV correction), SOH (capacity fade model). |
| Data logging | 1-second resolution; stored locally 90 days; uploaded to SCADA daily. |
| Alarm reporting | Pager/email to on-call engineer; critical alarms auto-dial. |

6. SCADA & COMMUNICATIONS

| Interface | Protocol | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Plant SCADA | Modbus TCP (over fibre) | Real-time monitoring of PCS, BMS, HVAC. |
| Grid dispatch | IEC 61850 (via RTU) | Active/reactive power setpoints from PHEDC control centre. |
| Remote access | VPN (site router) | NDRC engineering office, Lagos. |
| Data historian | PI Server (on-prem) | 1-min averages stored 5 years. |

documents.content:
7. THERMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

| Parameter | Specification | Remarks |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| Cooling type | Forced-air (HVAC) per container | 2 × 15 kW units per 20-ft container, duty/standby |
| Operating temp range | 15 °C – 35 °C (battery room) | De-rate above 30 °C per cell manufacturer curve |
| Setpoint | 25 °C ± 2 °C | Cooling engaged above 27 °C |
| Heating | 2 × 5 kW resistive heaters, thermostat controlled | For cold-start below 15 °C; not expected in PH climate |
| Airflow | 4,200 m³/h per container | Positive pressure, filtered (G4) |
| Temp alarm thresholds | High: 40 °C, High-high: 45 °C | High-high trips PCS and opens DC contactors |
| Humidity control | Dehumidifier, ≤ 70 % RH non-condensing | Condensation risk in wet season |
| Fire suppression | Novec 1230, 4 × 12 L cylinders per container | Discharge time 10 s; pre-discharge alarm 30 s |

HVAC units are sized for full-load heat rejection at 38 °C ambient (worst case, Apr–May). Each
container has independent control; loss of both HVAC units in one container triggers load
shedding to 50 % for that container within 15 minutes. Manual reset required after high-high
temp event.

8. SAFETY SYSTEMS

| System | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| DC isolation monitoring | Insulation resistance monitoring per rack; alarm at 100 kΩ, trip at 50 kΩ |
| Emergency stop | Local E-stop at each container door + remote trip from SCADA |
| Gas detection | H₂ and CO sensors per container, alarm at 25 % LEL |
| Ventilation | Passive vents + powered extraction on gas alarm |
| Arc flash protection | ARC detection on DC busbars, trip time < 5 ms |
| Ground fault protection | On AC side, 3-pole, 0.1 s trip |
| Personal safety | Signage, lockout/tagout procedure (NDRC-SOP-014), arc-rated PPE per NFPA 70E |
| Lightning protection | Type 1 + 2 surge arresters on AC and DC sides; earthing to 4 Ω max |

All safety systems tested quarterly per NDRC maintenance schedule. Gas detection sensors
calibrated every 6 months; last calibration 2023-02-14 (cert ref CAL-2023-0118).

9. OPERATING MODES

| Mode | Description | Transition time |
|------|-------------|-----------------|
| Grid-connected charge | Charge from grid at up to 8 MW, typically off-peak (00:00–05:00) | < 1 s to discharge |
| Grid-connected discharge | Discharge at up to 10 MW for peak shaving / backup | < 1 s to charge |
| Frequency response | Dynamic response to frequency deviation, ± 2 MW deadband ± 0.05 Hz | < 200 ms |
| Islanded / black-start | Supports islanded operation for designated feeder; black-start capability via PCS | < 100 ms (island transition) |
| Maintenance / standby | Offline, contactors open, HVAC running | Manual |

Frequency response mode is enabled per PHEDC dispatch instruction. Islanded operation tested
2023-01-18, 2 h run, load 3.2 MW, frequency held 50.0 ± 0.1 Hz.

10. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

| Interval | Activity | Responsible |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| Weekly | Visual inspection, HVAC filter check, alarm log review | Site technician |
| Monthly | Contact resistance check on DC terminals, torque check, BMS data review | Site technician |
| Quarterly | Safety system test, insulation resistance test, PCS performance check | Site engineer |
| Semi-annual | Rack capacity test (one rack), cell voltage spread check, HVAC service | Site engineer + OEM |
| Annual | Full capacity test (all racks), SOH calibration, torque re-check, thermal imaging | OEM + NDRC |

Annual capacity test due 2023-11; previous full capacity test 2022-11-28 gave 19.1 MWh usable
energy (within warranty tolerance). Spare parts held on site: 2 × HVAC blower motors, 1 × PCS
control board, 2 × CMC modules, 1 × dehumidifier.
